name: 14-handoff-edges-no-rules
description: The edges of handoff in a workspace with no rules, on three tasks. Task 1: a limit with no reset time holds the task with its Needs you item until a Verify of the login passes; a later limit with a reset time holds it with no item; a Verify then finds that login signed out, which leaves the hold with no due time, so the Account signed out item opens beside it; Sign in again resolves the item while the hold waits for the reset, and the builder's lease ends first, so the task returns to Ready with wait_ready naming credential_limit. Task 2: a limit hands off to the next login below, whose own limit then sends the work back to the seat's own login, which has reset; the reviewer's limit hands the review to a login of a provider that did not build the task. Task 3: a limit hands off past a limited login; the next limit comes while the seat's own login is still limited and the login between is available again, so the task is held with no item and the timer closes the hold at once; a reviewer found signed out with no candidate releases the review, another reviewer claims it and fails it, and the builder's fresh lease starts on its own login, which has reset. Task 1 is then cancelled.
covers: PRD test 8 and Build order, Handoff: one of the five golden traces for a workspace with no rules (milestone 3 plan HT-1, PRD R-7).

PRD Handoff, A limit with no reset time: credential_limit with the Limit with no reset time item, naming the login that stopped (milestone 3 plan HE-13); a passed Verify of it counts as a reading that shows capacity, clears the limit and closes the hold with hold.closed and inbox.resolved with no choice, and no credential event (milestone 3 plan HE-2, HE-10, HE-29).

Milestone 3 plan HE-11: a credential_limit hold whose one candidate with a reset time is found signed out by Verify keeps its reason; the Account signed out item opens beside it, naming that login; Sign in again resolves the item with the choice sign_in_again while the hold still waits for the reset (a passed check does not clear a limit that has a reset time, HE-2).

PRD Timers and leases and Handoff, Waiting on a limit: under credential_limit the lease keeps running, so the builder's lease ends at one lease length after the claim; task.lease_expired, then hold.closed with the wait_cause of the wait_ready step it opens (milestone 3 plan section 2.1, changed entries, HE-35): credential_limit, because the one builder that could take the task has no available candidate and none signed out, and the other two hold their tasks.

PRD Handoff, When a run hits a provider limit, and milestone 3 plan HE-4: the first available login below the stopped one takes over; when none below is available and the seat's own login has reset, the work goes back to the seat's own login at once with credential.switched and no hold.

Milestone 3 plan HE-4 and rules 6 and 8 of section 2.1: when the seat's own login is still limited and only a login between it and the stopped one is available, the hold opens with no item and is due at once; credential_hold_release closes it at the next sweep with its effective time at the hold's own, and the work moves to that login.

PRD Handoff, Reviews and jobs hand off like tasks: a reviewer's limit hands the review to the next login below with credential.switched naming the review; it lands on a provider that did not build the task (milestone 3 plan HE-41); a reviewer's sign-out with no candidate writes review.released, caused by credential.signed_out, opens no hold, and another reviewer claims the review.

PRD Handoff, What is recorded, and milestone 3 plan HE-14: a failed review gives the free builder a fresh lease on its first available candidate, and credential.switched is written because that is not the login last recorded for the task.

PRD Handoff, Which model continues, and milestone 3 plan HE-5: a handoff to another provider uses the credential's model (a Grok login's default, a Codex login's none); a handoff back to the seat's own provider uses the seat's model.
Milestone 3 plan HD-9: a continuing run announces again the criterion it was on, which is the seat's first event after the interruption; HE-17: a sign-out found by Verify starts no recovery time.
